summary: Set 111 Session 1: made the verification loop's bounds real. verify_session now REFUSES the round that would pass a bounded total (2 discovery-family passes, 2 remediation-review cycles, 2 classic rounds) before any metered call, unless the operator's --operator-authorized-round attestation is recorded in the new append-only per-session round ledger sN-rounds.jsonl; the K=2 discovery fan-out now sends two differently-framed prompts (spec-conformance / failure-scenario) over the same evidence instead of identical ones, with per-call evidence stamps and a discoveryLens recorded per finding; and a Minor-only round is a structural stop that is offered only the close command. Scope extension, operator-authorized mid-session: transports.copilot-cli.timeouts became a validated config block (total 300s -> 1200s) because this session's own MANDATORY verification could not complete inside the hardcoded ceiling.

reason.specifics: Session 2 builds acceptance criteria with baseline discrimination directly on top of S1's phase machinery in verify_session.py -- the round ledger, the enforced bounds and the discovery-lens fan-out are all load-bearing context for it, and the same orchestrator already holds the proposal's settled decisions. No capability or cost reason to switch; cross-provider independence is preserved where it matters, in the session-verification route.

notes: Verification loop actually run: discovery round 2 (K=2, both lenses) -> supplementary round 3 -> remediation round 1 -> remediation-review round 4 = VERIFIED (0 blocking; 1 fix-accepted, 1 duplicate-of, 1 accepted-with-modification). Within the newly enforced bounds: 2 discovery passes of 2, 1 remediation-review cycle of 2, no operator authorization needed.

Both discovery lenses independently reported the same Major (the undisclosed operator-authorized transport scope extension), which is convergence rather than added coverage; the supplementary pass produced the session's most valuable finding -- with a working reproduction -- that a clean supplementary round consumes a discovery pass but writes no envelope, so a third pass was accepted unauthorized. That defect was in S1's own headline deliverable and is fixed, with fails-before/passes-after evidence.

Operator-authorized scope extension (disclosed in s1-conventions.md with the full decision trail): the Copilot CLI transport's total dispatch ceiling was a hardcoded 300s with no config or env path, and a ~116KB session-verification bundle cannot complete inside it -- two total-timeout dispatches with nothing written, while a trivial prompt returned in 13s. The orchestrator refused to self-authorize and stopped to the operator, who chose the config knob. Known trade-off: a dispatch that streams then stalls can now occupy 20 minutes instead of 5; one that never starts still dies at first_byte_seconds=30.

UNRESOLVED, for the operator: s1-verification.md and a VERIFIED disposition appeared in this set's folder mid-session, written by something other than this session, with NO stamped row in router-metrics.jsonl. Per the operator's instruction it was treated as a third-party verification, left unedited (so it occupies round 1 and this session's own rounds are 2-4), and this session closed only on its own stamped evidence. One substantive point from it was acted on (the VERIFIED-plus-NITS exit wording). A SECOND occurrence is to be treated as verification running out of band and investigated -- possibly a path-aware CLI process launching verification in parallel.

Suite: 3,478 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped locally, after the last code change. 31 tests were deselected as pre-existing environmental failures on this seat, in two classes, neither touching a module this session changed: missing DABBLER_OPENAI_API_KEY (drift-guard model-inventory checks, proven pre-existing by a stashed-baseline re-run) and real Copilot CLI dispatch total-timeouts in tests that shell out to the CLI.

Deferred to later sessions by the spec, not by omission: acceptance criteria with baseline discrimination (S2), the decision-rights rubric and decision journal (S3), and the ceremony pass including the artifact-necessity review and the guided-look UAT format (S4). requiresUAT is a set-level flag S4 dogfoods; S1 ships no UI surface.
